*   Advisor: Selin Gülgöz, PhD 

**B.A., Honors Psychology; Minor in Chemistry** | 2022   
*New York University*   

*   Thesis: Who do you want to be friends with? Examining children’s gender affiliative preferences 
*   Advisor: Marjorie Rhodes, PhD 

---

## Technical & Methodological Skills

*   **Data Analysis:** R, SQL, Python, SPSS, JASP 
*   **Programming:** HTML, JavaScript 
*   **Experimental Design & Software:** Qualtrics, Salesforce, SurveyMonkey, Datavyu, Keynote, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator 
*   **Languages:** Spanish (native), English (native), Italian (conversational) 

---

## Research Experience

**Impact Research Intern** | Newsela (Summer 2026) 

*   Designed and executed BigQuery SQL analyses on large-scale educational datasets using a dbt/GCP data warehouse architecture.

*   Produced a strategic research report identifying data infrastructure gaps and evidence-based recommendations for improving platform support for bilingual/multilingual students.

**Research Intern** | EmbraceRace (2025–2026) 

*   Led end-to-end survey administration and project management for an original study with a nationally representative sample of 1,000 U.S. parents.

**Researcher** | The Research and Insights Lab (TRAIL) (2024–Present) 

*   Conducted end-to-end mixed methods research involving survey optimization, data collection, and statistical analyses (factor analyses, ANOVAs, semantic/thematic analyses).

**Graduate Research Apprentice** | Social Thinkers Lab, Fordham University (2023–Present)

*   Led independent research projects and conducted advanced statistical analyses in R for cognitive and behavioral data. 

*Previous roles include Graduate Researcher at CoDE Lab (Fordham), Lab Manager and Undergraduate Research Assistant at CDSC Lab (NYU).* 

---

## Teaching Experience

## Mentorship & Leadership

*   **Student Rep, Fordham Applied Developmental Psychology Executive Council:** Advocated for the 2023 ADP doctoral cohort and enabled active communication between students and faculty.
*   **Mentor, Fordham Psychology Peer Mentoring Program:** Mentored undergraduate students from traditionally underrepresented backgrounds in Psychology (2023–2025).
*   **Research Ambassador, NYU College of Arts & Sciences:** Conducted workshops on engaging in research and offered feedback on NYU DURF grant applications (2021–2022).
*   **Mentor, NYU Academic Achievement Program (AAP):** (2019–2022).
*   **Research Fellow, NYU CSTEP:** Led workshops on reading scientific papers and mentored younger students (2019–2022).

---

## Select Publications & Technical Reports

*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Gülgöz, S. (Revise & Resubmit, Developmental Science). *Status reasoning about bilingualism and accents across development*. 
*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Rucinski, C. (In progress). *Color-conscious versus color-evasive ideologies in a nationally representative sample of US parents*. 
*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Gülgöz, S. (In progress). *The role of accents as cues to trust and learning*. 
*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Landrigan, J., (2026). *Bilingual and multilingual student outcomes on Newsela: A matched comparison study of reading growth using platform engagement and NWEA MAP assessment data*. Newsela (Internal report). 
*   Hoxie, A.M., **De Leon Escobar, A.** (2025). *League of Young Inventors: Evaluation Report*. Research and Insights Lab.

## Select Conference Presentations

*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Gülgöz, S. (2026, May). *Monolingual children’s status-based evaluations of bilingual speakers*. Talk presented at the 2026 Association for Psychological Science (APS) Annual Meeting, Barcelona, SP. (Poster also accepted) .
*   **De Leon Escobar, A.**, Gülgöz, S. (2026, April). *Monolingual children’s status-based evaluations of bilingual speakers*. Poster presented at the 2026 Cognitive Development Society (CDS) Biennial Meeting, Montréal, CA .
